scenario.fault_family: link cut (both fabric uplinks of one leaf)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) reports a total outage: nothing across the
fabric responds, and pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) cannot reach pc_0_1 either.
pc_0_1 CAN still ping its own gateway 10.0.1.1, and leaf_router_0_1
itself is up and reachable on its console -- its FRR daemons are all
running. Both of its BGP sessions to the spines are gone. Diagnose.

injection.command:
ip link set eth0 down
  ip link set eth1 down

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP
ip -br link show eth1 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_1 eth0 and eth1 -- BOTH fabric
  uplinks: eth0 (172.16.0.7/31, link subnet 172.16.0.6/31) to
  spine_router_0_0 and eth1 (172.16.0.11/31, link subnet
  172.16.0.10/31) to spine_router_0_1
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_1's only paths into the CLOS fabric are its
  two spine uplinks. With both interfaces down, both BGP sessions drop
  and the leaf can neither learn 10.0.0.0/24 nor deliver its own
  10.0.1.0/24 traffic anywhere -- the CLOS redundancy is defeated
  because BOTH members of the redundant pair are down. The host-facing
  port eth2 (10.0.1.1/24) is untouched, so pc_0_1 still reaches its
  gateway but nothing beyond it. Note this is the one link-fault shape
  where redundancy does not save the leaf; a single downed uplink
  would only degrade redundancy.
Localization: leaf_router_0_1
Root cause: both spine-facing interfaces (eth0, eth1) down on
  leaf_router_0_1
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` and `ip link set eth1 up` on
  leaf_router_0_1; both BGP sessions re-establish on their own.
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth0 up && ip link set eth1 up` on leaf_router_0_1. Once
the uplinks are UP the sessions to both spines come back and pc_0_1
regains fabric reachability.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The outage is caused by loss of both uplinks from leaf_router_0_1 to the spines (L2/link layer issue, not an FRR problem). On leaf_router_0_1, the upstream interfaces are down: ip link shows eth0 and eth1 in state DOWN, and ethtool reports “Link detected: no” on both. Consequently, BGP on leaf_router_0_1 shows both spine neighbors stuck in Active (no TCP session), and the leaf has no routes beyond its local subnet 10.0.1.0/24. This explains why pc_0_1 can still ping its gateway (10.0.1.1 on eth2) but nothing else.

From the spine side, reachability to the leaf’s point-to-point addresses is broken: ping to 172.16.0.7 (spine_router_0_0→leaf eth0) and 172.16.0.11 (spine_router_0_1→leaf eth1) fails with ARP “INCOMPLETE,” confirming L2 adjacency is gone. The rest of the fabric is healthy: leaf_router_0_0 has both BGP sessions up, and the spines have routes to 10.0.0.0/24.

Localization: leaf_router_0_1 interfaces eth0 (to spine_router_0_0 eth2, 172.16.0.6/31-172.16.0.7/31) and eth1 (to spine_router_0_1 eth2, 172.16.0.10/31-172.16.0.11/31). Root cause: both uplink interfaces on leaf_router_0_1 are administratively/physically down.

Corrective fix: bring the uplinks up and ensure they auto-up at boot:
- On leaf_router_0_1: ip link set dev eth0 up; ip link set dev eth1 up
- Verify ethtool shows “Link detected: yes,” then confirm BGP neighbors establish (show ip bgp summary)
- Persist the interface state in the host’s network config so they remain up across restarts.

The agent correctly recommends bringing eth0 and eth1 up on leaf_router_0_1 (ip link set ... up), verifying link and BGP session establishment, and persisting the config so the uplinks remain up.
